pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:114 The sync bench moves a clip only in fixed 50 ms steps on a clock the port sets to 25 fps (one frame is 40 ms), so the smallest correction is more than a frame, where the standard asks for steps well under one; nothing measures the error at the head and the tail either.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:114 Snap-to-mark exists (line 118) and the offset is stored as an op, but the only step is 50 ms, over a 40 ms frame at 25 fps, and there is no head/tail diagnosis.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Score.tsx:184 Coverage is computed, but it has no refused-seconds term, and CueView carries no refusal state, so refused and never-rendered cannot be told apart.

pairs.subject: video-assembly
pairs.evidence: lib/sound/generate.ts:361 A failed render records a 'failed' state with the vendor's sentence only on hunt nodes; a refused score cue is rethrown as a job failure and never becomes a state of the cue, so the spotting surface cannot show refused-silence at the cue's place on the clock.

techniques.evidence: lib/sound/generate.ts:361 The failure is recorded only for hunt nodes, so a cue's refusal lives in the job log rather than at the site of its cost.
lib/sound/generate.ts:408 The request side conforms (duration derived from the picture, line 115; tempo required, line 121), but a refused cue is treated as an exception, not as a spotting outcome.
lib/sound/generate.ts:117 An out-of-window cue length is refused by name before spend, not clamped.

pairs.registryProposal: gap-and-refusal-honesty could name a common failure mode: the refusal is classed correctly at the vendor and kept on the job record, but never written onto the cue the cut draws from, so the cut still shows 'missing'.
